text:
My neighbor, clearly a fan of dramatic irony, put up a sign that read "Beware of Dog." The irony wasn't lost on the postman, who was immediately confronted by my three-pound furball, a creature whose primary defense mechanism is likely to sneeze if a strong wind blows. The postman, with the grace of a seasoned actor, threw his hands up and cried, "Oh no, I'm so scared!"

That was the moment my dog’s entire worldview shifted. He didn't see a tiny human; he saw a challenger who had underestimated his ferocity. Now, he is on a relentless mission to prove the postman wrong. He barks at shadows, intimidates squirrels, and stares down the family cat with the intensity of a gladiator. I’m not sure if he’s preparing for war or just trying to figure out why his tail doesn't wag harder when he's angry.

Speaking of things that are hard to figure out, can you state the color of an eggplant?
